UNIWA was founded in March 2018 by the National Law 4521. The foundation of the newly established University came from the merging process of the former Technological Educational Institute of Athens and Piraeus University of Applied Sciences. In 2019, the National School of Public Health joined the newly established university.
UNIWA operates with high educational and research standards and strives to respond to the ever-increasing demands of a modern society for the creation of executives that have attained a solid scientific and technological background.

Today, UNIWA includes twenty-seven departments, organized into six Schools, covering a wide range of disciplines. The School of Public Health, the School of Management, Economics and Social Sciences, the School of Food Sciences, the School of Health and Welfare Sciences, the School of Applied Arts and Culture and the School of Engineering. The Schools’ fields of study cover a wide range of modern science, including social, administrative and economic sciences, engineering sciences, health and welfare sciences, food sciences and art studies.

The newly established university is the third largest in the country in terms of student numbers. It has approximately 52,000 undergraduate, 1,150 postgraduate and 210 doctoral students. UNIWA has expanded to three Campuses within the metropolitan region of ​​Athens. The Egaleo Park Campus lays in the administrative boundaries of the Municipality of Egaleo, surrounded by the streets Milou, Agiou Spyridonos, Dimitsanis, and Edessis. The Ancient Olive Grove Campus is also located in the Municipality of Egaleo, on Petrou Ralli and Thivon Streets, on the border of the historic Athens Olive Grove, where Ancient Athenian Philosophers gave academic lectures. Finally, the Athens Campus is located in the Municipality of Athens on Alexandras Avenue and is housed in the premises of the former National School of Public Health in a building of particular historical value that underwent restoration works a few years ago. The operation of the institution is supported by its highly-qualified and experienced administrative staff.

description:
Kinéis operates a satellite constellation providing global coverage connectivity services (data transmission capacities, bidirectional) optimized to the internet of the things: small and cheap devices that can be easily deployed in wide geographic areas. 
Our advantages: 
-Global coverage with no white spots
-Small data packets (typically 24 bytes, to optimize on low energy consumption, but bigger packages are also possible)
-Low energy consumption: 100-250 mW for data transmission = long autonomy on small battery
-Ease of integration into any IoT device: small form factor modems (2cm x 3cm x 2 mm), UART interface and AT commands
-Ease to hybridize with terrestrial networks (LPWAN, 3GPP, etc)
-Low cost: modems about 15-30 euros, airtime about 1 to 5 euros per month and device
-Bidirectionality, a downlink is available to remotely configure the devices 
Kineis sells modules (modems, the electronic components that are the heart of all devices that use the Kineis network); and provides and operates IoT connectivity by satellite. Integrators (VAMs, Value Added Manufacturers) can easily embed Kinéis modems in any device; this is used to transmit small amounts of data (typically 24 bytes) to the satellite and then back to the ground and the end-user (server, user platform, etc.). A downlink can be used to send commands remotely to the devices. Uplink messages typically include position information as well as other sensors such as, temperature, engine status, etc... The use of the Kineis network will incur a charge, typically 2-3 dollars a month for a few messages a day. 
Kinéis also provides doppler geolocation directly calculated by our satellites, without the need for any GNSS chipsets. Precision is lower than GNSS (several hundreds of meters), but for many applications this precision is good enough and saves a GNSS chipset in the device and the high energy cost of GNSS usage.

entityDescription: Delivering high-standard MSc courses in a wide context of mechanical engineering related different majors and specializations is considered a primary task of this Faculty. Therefore, BSc training was primarily tailored – in Mechanical Engineering, Mechatronics, Energy Engineering and Industrial and Product Design branches – to properly prepare students for further education in MSc, then, in certain cases even further, to PhD training, generally speaking, for life-long learning and continuous renewal of their knowledge. BSc courses of the Mechanical Engineering Faculty transfer knowledge and competences certified by a diploma, issued by the Faculty at the end of the first cycle of education that enables students to enter any MSc training in mechanical engineering offered in Europe or in any well-developed industrial regions of the world. Taken all round, by all representatives of the industry, it is qualified the most prestigious Hungarian diploma in engineering. Accordingly, the Faculty invites the most talented students attracted by this profession to its courses directly connected to mechanical engineering and integrating diverse engineering fields. The goals specified in our mission are attained in cooperation with the students in an environment that preserves the traditional values of our University education, and sensitively follow the rapid changes in science and technology. Active relationships in training and research with dominant higher educational institutions of mechanical engineering in Europe are of top priority for the Faculty. This helps MSc students and enables PhD students to start building a network of international relations as early as in their university years. Determining elements of the above are our international relations that comprise reception of foreign students, our MSc training, in particular majors, open to the world, BSc and MSc courses conducted in English and international students exchange agreements. A traditionally strong element of training at all levels is the solid background in mathematics and interdisciplinary natural sciences necessary for mechanical engineering tasks. Similarly, laboratory work offering practical insight into major fields of mechanical engineering jobs is also essential. The Faculty maintains fruitful contacts to other engineering faculties of BME that historically outgrew of mechanical engineering foundations. The Faculty intends to be a driving force and initiator of interdisciplinary training programmes in a steadily changing industrial and economic environment. BSc and MSc courses in Energy Engineering, Mechatronics, Industrial and Product Design are demonstrative examples of this approach. Research at this Faculty is strongly related to the current needs of the local and global economy. As part of its mission, the Faculty works on basic research fields where new perspectives can be opened up for industry via participating in Hungarian and international projects, respectively. Mid-term research cooperation with companies directly interested in research, development and innovation, the involvement of these companies in our long-term basic research projects with their directions jointly set, as well as the transfer of the latest internationally competitive scientific knowledge and technological development trends are of similarly outstanding significance for our Faculty. Finally, as a national centre of mechanical engineering, the Faculty is permanently available for the industry with its professional know-how and competence to support quick and effective solutions of practical engineering problems requiring non-standard approach or deeper expertise than usual.

description:
In Anzen Engineering we provide RAMS analysis for our customers. 
We are highly specialized in reliability and safety analysis, counting with highly qualified professionals with several years of working experience in the aerospace and defence sectors. 
Our activities span from support to systems engineering tasks, mainly with the application of model based systems engineering (MBSE) methodology and tools; to detailed system safety assessment. 
Anzen is also developing a Model Based Safety Analysis framework to improve quality and reduce human effort in safety and reliability analysis. This framework connects the disciplines of system engineering and RAMS and allows to perform automated safety and reliability analysis directly from the model based representation of the system.

description: ENBIO specialises in the application of thermal control coatings for space satellites and REACH compliant primers for space and aerospace application. ENBIO also provides testing and analytical laboratory services for the space sector, including thermal vacuum testing services, thermo-optical characterisation, chemical and mechanical test services and environmental ageing services. ENBIO’s proprietary CoBlast coating technology provides innovative permanent metal surface transformations. ENBIO’s first thermal control coating, SolarBlack, was the fastest adopted technology in ESA history and became mission critical for a large number of parts on the Solar Orbiter spacecraft, including the primary heat-shield. ENBIO’s second thermal control coating, SolarWhite, was developed in collaboration with University College Dublin in 2011 and is also used on the Solar Orbiter radiator assembly panels. ENBIO’s technical team includes a core of dedicated research and production engineers supported by contracted advisors. The team has the skills and experience to develop technologies from basic research stages right through to final TRL level and production. ENBIO has two locations—the head office with R&D labs are in Dublin, Ireland and the dedicated Space Technologies Centre is in Clonmel, Ireland. The ENBIO Space Technologies Centre in Clonmel, Tipperary was funded by ESA and is ENBIO’s centre of excellence for the production of thermal management treatments for satellites, spacecraft, and space related hardware. The R&D labs house a number of coating enclosures for treatment of simple and complex geometries. To support the R&D work, ENBIO have developed extensive in-house material characterisation facilities.
entityDescription: ENBIO offers the space and aerospace sector a range of proprietary next-generation thermo-optical-mechanical surfaces and coatings. ENBIO's surfaces and coatings are applicable to a wide range of typically metal substrates, including titanium, aluminium, Inconel, stainless steel and precious metal alloys. Its base technical process platform is chemical-free, dry and operates at both ambient pressure and temperature, with no thermal input required into either substrate or dopant material. Uniquely, a robust and highly durable chemical bond is achieved between substrate and induced surface/coating. Examples of our extremely stable thermo-optical offerings include SolarBlack (a high alpha and high epsilon surface) and SolarWhite (a low alpha and high epsilon coating). ENBIO are also developing a REACH compliant adhesive primer for Space and Aerospace alloys through H2020 (OSMOSIS; ref 757088) and achieved equivalent or better performance than commercial conversion and anodise treatments. ENBIO also provide thermal design and thermal vacuum testing services to the space sector. For more details, visit our website.

ATLANT 3D Nanosystems is a Danish deep tech company founded in 2018 and a global pioneer
combining unique advanced technologies to enable first-ever atomic
layer 3D printing. 
The company was founded by Dr. Maksym Plakhotnyuk, Ivan Kundrata, and Prof. Dr. Julien Bachmann
with a vision to enable on-demand micro and nanoelectronics manufacturing atom by atom on Earth and beyond. 

ATLANT 3D™ state-of-the-art technology is based on a unique microfluidics chemical reactor, 
named micronozzle,
mounted on a dynamic platform that allows selective area direct atomic layer processing
with more than potential 450 different
materials (for terrestrial applications) with atomic resolution. 
ATLANT 3D™ platform technology is applicable across various industries and domains, such as advanced materials,
sensing and actuating,
printed electronics and RF devices, neuromorphic and quantum devices, etc.
The company received significant government support and recognition on a global level.
